newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Ciampi quoted as saying rate cut possible.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Ciampi quoted as saying rate cut possible.

text.p: Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said in an interview the recent fall in inflation would open the way for a drop in interest rates.
"The decline in inflation certainly makes a reduction in interest rates possible," Ciampi said in an interview with Il Mondo magazine, released ahead of publication.

"This would prevent the strange phenomenon of falling inflation being coupled with a real rise in interest rates at a time when (economic) growth is moderate and one cannot see the motives for (inflation) to pick up again," Ciampi added.
Preliminary data indicated that inflation would fall to 1.7 percent year-on-year in April from 2.2 percent in March.
Ciampi said that, net of statistical distortions, Italian inflation was currently running at around 1.1 percent. The official discount rate is 6.75 percent.
"From the performance of wage inflation, the cost of raw materials, above all petrol, it is clear that the (inflationary) tendency is destined to last," Ciampi said. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
